question: Can the pinned original Cano generate_environments.py emit one readable native mesh/axis/SDF bundle in the frozen E1 environment, and are its exported axis/tunnel labels valid enough to serve as topology ground truth?
method: Use the already selected and frozen E1 environment without reinstalling dependencies. Run the original scripts/generate_environments.py directly and unmodified for exactly one temporary environment with three requested grown tunnels and one requested connector, no GUI plot, and a 30-minute timeout. Then audit the four original files, mesh readability/manifold diagnostics, SDF references, axis schema, cross-tunnel label conflicts, unexported return values, and source integrity. Generate one deterministic full-export mesh-axis diagnostic preview. Do not repair outputs or count the smoke as a dataset world.
baseline: The compatibility matrix proved E1 process executability for snippet_2.py but exported no world. Source audit already predicts that generate_environments.py ignores connector failures, mishandles grown return tuples, and repeats global axis points under each tunnel ID; these predictions must be tested rather than hidden.

user_authorization.scope: One original Cano native-export smoke only: exactly one temporary environment with three requested grown tunnels and one requested connector; no adapter, batch, Isaac, LiDAR, labels, training, or M-TARE changes.

acceptance_criteria: The selected E1 package freeze matches the compatibility evidence and pip check remains clean; no dependency installation or environment mutation occurs.
Source remote, commit, tracked status, and original entrypoint SHA-256 match before and after execution.
Exactly one original native export attempt is made with one requested environment, three grown tunnels, one connector, no plot, and no overwrite flag.
mesh.obj, axis.txt, fta_dist.txt, and model.sdf are all present; mesh.obj is non-empty and readable, and SDF references that exact mesh.
Mesh executability and topology-GT validity are judged separately. Native mesh PASS must not hide missing graph export, ignored generator failures, or conflicting per-tunnel axis labels.
axis.txt is rejected as per-tunnel ground truth if identical axis coordinates carry multiple tunnel IDs, or marked unverified if fewer than two tunnel IDs are available.
The only preview overlays actual exported mesh vertices and all axis rows and explicitly states that it cannot prove topology validity or navigation feasibility.
The smoke contributes zero formal dataset worlds and produces no adapter, batch, Isaac, LiDAR, labels, training, ROS, benchmark, or M-TARE change.
stop_conditions: E1 environment missing, freeze mismatch, or pip check failure
Source remote, commit, clean status, or entrypoint hash mismatch
Original export exceeds 1800 seconds or exits nonzero
More than one environment or export attempt would be required
Disk use would exceed 3 GB for native outputs
expected_evidence: Exact original command, E1 freeze hash, source pre/post hashes, stdout/stderr, duration, and exit code
Original mesh.obj, axis.txt, fta_dist.txt, and model.sdf from exactly one temporary environment
Machine-readable mesh, SDF, axis-schema, cross-tunnel-label-conflict, and missing-topology-export audit
One deterministic actual-export mesh-axis diagnostic preview with provenance
Explicit zero formal-dataset, LiDAR, label, and training counts and a PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL claim boundary

estimated_cost.compute: CPU-only original Cano point-cloud/Poisson mesh generation and offline validation using the existing E1 environment; no network install, GPU, Isaac, LiDAR, or training.
